stages.label: Non-Cooperation + Khilafat (1920-22)
stages.detail: Gandhi's first all-India mass mobilisation. Khilafat triggers, Calcutta Special Session Sept 1920 accepts NCM, Nagpur Dec 1920 changes Congress creed. Congress Volunteer Corps, boycott of schools/courts/foreign cloth, Tilak Swaraj Fund (Rs 1 crore oversubscribed). Ali Brothers nationwide tour. Prince of Wales visit riots Nov 1921. Chauri Chaura 5 Feb 1922 → withdrawal 12 Feb 1922. Ended with Gandhi's 6-year jail sentence March 1922. Peasant spillover (Avadh Kisan Sabha, Eka), Moplah Rebellion Aug 1921 in Malabar.

stages.label: Swarajists vs No-Changers (1922-27)
stages.detail: Post-NCM Congress crisis. Gaya Session Dec 1922 defeated council-entry 1748-890. C.R. Das + Motilal formed Swaraj Party Jan 1923. Delhi Special Session Sept 1923 compromised. 1923 Elections — Swarajists won 42/101. Vithalbhai Patel CLA President 1925. C.R. Das death June 1925. Belgaum Dec 1924 reunification under Gandhi. Kaliparaj/Raniparaj uplift work. Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 — Patel earns "Sardar" title. Constructive programme (ashrams, khadi, Hindu-Muslim unity, anti-untouchability).

stages.label: Revolutionary Terrorists (1922-34)
stages.detail: HRA founded at Kanpur Oct 1924 (Bismil, Chatterjea, Sanyal) — Kakori Robbery Aug 1925 → Kakori Conspiracy Case → Ashfaqulla, Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri hanged 1927. Reorganised as HSRA at Ferozeshah Kotla Sept 1928. Lajpat Rai death Nov 1928 → Saunders Assassination Dec 1928. Assembly Bomb 8 April 1929. Jatin Das hunger-strike death Sept 1929. Philosophy of the Bomb (1930). Lahore Conspiracy Case → Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru hanged 23 March 1931. Chandrashekhar Azad shoots self at Alfred Park Feb 1931. Surya Sen's Chittagong Armoury Raid 18 April 1930 → Jalalabad battle 22 April → 3-year guerrilla → Surya Sen hanged Jan 1934. Female revolutionaries: Pritilata Waddedar, Kalpana Dutt, Bina Das, Santi Ghosh, Suniti Chowdhury.

stages.label: Gathering Storm + Civil Disobedience (1927-31)
stages.detail: Simon Commission announcement Nov 1927, boycott from Feb 3 1928. Madras Session Dec 1927 snap Purna Swaraj resolution. All-Parties Conference 1928 → Nehru Report. Jinnah's 14 Points March 1929. Irwin Declaration Oct 1929 + Delhi Manifesto Nov 1929. Lahore Session Dec 1929 — Purna Swaraj. Independence Day Pledge 26 Jan 1930. Gandhi's 11-point ultimatum Jan 31 1930. Dandi March 12 March - 6 April 1930. Khudai Khidmatgars + Peshawar uprising April 1930. Sholapur Uprising May 1930. Dharasana Salt Raid 21 May 1930 (Sarojini Naidu). First Round Table Conference Nov 1930. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 5 March 1931. Chowkidara Tax Refusal, no-rent UP, forest law defiance, chunks of women's participation.

stages.label: Karachi to Wardha (1931-34)
stages.detail: Karachi Session March 1931 — Fundamental Rights + National Economic Programme resolutions. Second RTC Aug-Dec 1931. Gandhi's "last cup of poison" journey, return empty-handed. Willingdon Viceroy. 4 Jan 1932 pre-emptive crackdown → CD Round 2 1932-34 → crushed by mid-1932. Communal Award 16 Aug 1932. Gandhi's Epic Fast 20 Sept 1932 → Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932. Harijan Sewak Sangh Sept 1932. Harijan Tour Nov 1933 - July 1934 (20,000 km). Poona bomb on Gandhi June 1934. Second CD withdrawal April 1934. Third RTC 1932.

stages.label: Rise of the Left Wing (1925-39)
stages.detail: Indian socialist+communist formation. Tashkent CPI 1920 (M.N. Roy). Kanpur Bolshevik Case 1924. CPI founded Kanpur Dec 1925. Workers+Peasants' Parties 1927. Meerut Conspiracy 1929-33. Bhagat Singh's Marxist turn 1929-31. CPI banned 1934. CSP founded at Bombay Oct 1934 (JP Narayan, Narendra Dev, Minoo Masani, Achyut Patwardhan). Dutt-Bradley Thesis 1936 → CPI re-enters Congress. Nehru presided Lucknow 1936 (socialist presidential address) + Faizpur Dec 1936 (first rural session). National Planning Committee 1938. Forward Bloc 1939 (Bose). Royists. Left bloc fights 1936-37 office-acceptance debate.

stages.label: Working Class + Trade Unionism (1918-47)
stages.detail: Ahmedabad TLA founded by Gandhi 1918. AITUC 1920 (Lala Lajpat Rai first president, Dewan Chaman Lal Gen Sec). 1919-22 railway strikes, Prince of Wales boycott involving 1.4 lakh Bombay workers. 1928 Jharia AITUC Communist dominance + Bombay Textile Strike April-Sept 1928. Girni Kamgar Union. Sholapur Uprising May 1930. 1929 Public Safety Bill + Trade Disputes Act + Meerut Case. Royal Commission on Labour 1929 (Whitley). Post-1937 Congress Ministries — rise in unions. WWII: Bombay anti-war strike Oct 1939 (90,000 workers). CPI People's War line from Dec 1941. 1942 Tata Steel 13-day strike, Ahmedabad textile 3.5-month strike. INA trials solidarity. RIN Mutiny Feb 1946. All India P&T Strike 1946.

stages.label: Peasant Movements (1918-47)
stages.detail: UP Kisan Sabha 1918. Oudh Kisan Sabha Oct 1920 (Baba Ramchandra, Nehru). Eka Movement 1921-22. Moplah Rebellion Aug-Dec 1921 (Ali Musaliar, Kunhammed Haji). Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 (Sardar Patel). Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha 1929 (Sahajanand). Chowkidara Tax Refusal 1930. All India Kisan Sabha founded Lucknow April 1936. Karshaka Sangham (Kerala). N.G. Ranga's Indian Peasants Institute Andhra 1933. Andhra Long March 1938 (2,000 kisans, 1,500 miles). Bakasht Lands Struggle (Bihar 1938-39). Punjab Kisan Committee 1937 → Lahore Kisan Morcha 1939. Bengal Famine 1943 relief. Tebhaga Movement 1946-47. Punnapra-Vayalar 1946. Telangana Rebellion 1946-51.

stages.label: Akali + Temple Entry + Social Reform (1920-47)
stages.detail: Akali Movement 1920-25 — SGPC + Shiromani Akali Dal Dec 1920, Nankana Tragedy Feb 1921, Keys Affair Oct 1921, Guru-Ka-Bagh Aug 1922, Jaito 1923, Sikh Gurdwaras Act July 1925. Vaikom Satyagraha 1924-25 (K.P. Kesava Menon, Periyar, Gandhi). Guruvayur Satyagraha 1931-32 (K. Kelappan, A.K. Gopalan, P. Krishna Pillai). Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation Nov 1936. Madras Temple Entry Act 1938 (Rajagopalachari). Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929. Gandhi's Harijan work. Women's movements (AIWC 1927, Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali, Sucheta Kripalani).

stages.label: Princely States Freedom Struggle (1927-48)
stages.detail: Praja Mandals (States Peoples' associations) from 1920. All India States' Peoples Conference founded Dec 1927 (Baiwantrai Mehta, Manikial Kothari, G.R. Abhayankar). Congress 1920 Nagpur Resolution on states. Tripuri 1939 resolution identifying Congress with states peoples. Nehru President AISPC Ludhiana 1939. Rajkot Satyagraha 1938-39 (Gandhi + Kasturba). Hyderabad State Congress 1938 (Swami Ramananda Tirtha). Kashmir Quit Kashmir May 1946 (Sheikh Abdullah). Travancore (C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar), Jaipur, Mysore, Patiala struggles. Integration of Princely States Aug-Oct 1947 (Patel + V.P. Menon). Instrument of Accession. Operation Polo Sept 1948 (Hyderabad).

stages.label: Indian Capitalists + National Movement (1927-47)
stages.detail: FICCI founded 1927 (G.D. Birla, Purshottamdas Thakurdas). Boycotted First RTC 1930 for lack of Congress participation. Opposed Public Safety Bill 1928 (capitalists+Congress united). 1930 CD support but with warnings against "disastrous after-effects". GD Birla's mediation in Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931. Capitalist pushback on Left radicalisation 1935-36. Indian capitalists' 5 Aug 1942 letter urging "granting political freedom" to avert Quit India. Bombay Plan 1944 (Thakurdas, JRD Tata, Birla, Ardeshir Dalal, Sri Ram, Kasturbhai Lalbhai, A.D. Shroff, John Mathai). Post-War Economic Development Committee 1942.

stages.label: 28 Months of Congress Rule (1937-39)
stages.detail: 1937 Provincial Elections — Congress won 716/1161, majority in 6+2 provinces. Parliamentary Sub-Committee (Patel, Azad, Rajendra Prasad) coordinated ministries. Civil liberties restored. Congress Election Manifesto 1936 implemented partially. Haripura Session Feb 1938 (Bose first presidency) + Haripura Panels by Nandalal Bose. Tripuri Crisis March 1939 — Bose re-elected vs Sitaramayya 1580-1377, forced to resign. Forward Bloc 3 May 1939. WWII outbreak 1 Sept 1939 — Linlithgow declared India at war without consultation. Congress Ministries resigned Oct-Nov 1939. Muslim League "Deliverance Day" 22 Dec 1939.

stages.label: WWII + Individual Satyagraha (1939-42)
stages.detail: Ministries resignation Oct 1939. Ramgarh March 1940. August Offer 8 Aug 1940 (Linlithgow). Individual Satyagraha from 17 Oct 1940 — Vinoba Bhave first, Nehru second. 25,000 convicted by May 1941. Pearl Harbor 7 Dec 1941. Japan overruns SE Asia, occupies Rangoon March 1942. CWC Dec 1941 offers cooperation; Gandhi designates Nehru as successor Jan 1942. Cripps Mission March-April 1942 — Dominion Status + provincial opt-out (implicit Pakistan) + no real transfer. Congress rejection; Gandhi "post-dated cheque".

stages.label: Quit India + INA (1942-45)
stages.detail: AICC Gowalia Tank 8 Aug 1942 — Quit India Resolution + "Do or Die" speech. 9 Aug arrests. Aruna Asaf Ali hoists flag. Underground movement: Patwardhan, Aruna, Lohia, Sucheta, JP (escaped Nov 1942), Biju Patnaik. Usha Mehta's Congress Radio Aug-Nov 1942. Parallel governments: Ballia (Chittu Pande), Tamluk Jatiya Sarkar Dec 1942, Satara Prati Sarkar 1943-45 (Nana Patil). Gandhi's 21-Day Fast Feb-March 1943. Rash Behari Bose + Indian Independence League Tokyo 1942. First INA (Mohan Singh) Sept 1942. Bose takes charge July 1943. Azad Hind Government 21 Oct 1943 Singapore. Rani of Jhansi Regiment (Lakshmi Sahgal). Imphal-Kohima campaign 1944. Chalo Delhi, Moirang flag-hoisting.

stages.label: Post-War Upsurge to Partition (1945-47)
stages.detail: Labour govt elected UK July 1945. Indian leaders released June 1945. Simla Conference + Wavell Plan June-July 1945 — failed. INA Red Fort Trials Nov 1945 (Shah Nawaz, Sahgal, Dhillon) with Bhulabhai Desai leading defence. INA Day 12 Nov, INA Week 5-11 Nov 1945. Upsurges: Calcutta 21 Nov 1945, Rashid Ali Feb 1946, RIN Mutiny 18-23 Feb 1946 (HMIS Talwar, B.C. Dutt, Karachi). 1945-46 Elections (Congress 91% general, League 100% Muslim). Cabinet Mission announced 22 Jan 1946, arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Plan 16 May 1946 (three-tier federation). Congress accepted with reservations; League accepted 6 June, withdrew July. Direct Action Day 16 Aug 1946 + Great Calcutta Killing. Noakhali Oct 1946. Bihar riots. Gandhi's peace walks. Interim Government 2 Sept 1946. League joined 26 Oct. Attlee statement 20 Feb 1947. Mountbatten arrived 22 March 1947. Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947. Radcliffe Commission. Indian Independence Act 18 July 1947. 14-15 Aug 1947 midnight — Tryst with Destiny, Partition, Independence.

stages.label: Constitution Making (1946-49)
stages.detail: M.N. Roy idea 1934. CA demand in INC from 1935, Cripps 1942. Cabinet Mission Plan May 1946 framework. CA elections July-Aug 1946 (INC 208, League 73, independents 15). CA first meeting 9 Dec 1946 — Sachchidananda Sinha temp president; Rajendra Prasad elected 11 Dec; HC Mukherjee + VT Krishnamachari VPs. Objectives Resolution by Nehru 13 Dec 1946, adopted 22 Jan 1947. Independence Act changes Aug 1947 — CA became sovereign + Dominion legislature; Muslim League Pakistan withdrawal; strength 299. 8 major committees; Drafting Committee 29 Aug 1947 (Ambedkar + 6 others). B.N. Rau constitutional advisor. First draft Feb 1948, second Oct 1948. 7,653 amendments. Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949, effective 26 Jan 1950.

stages.label: Rise of Communalism (1920-47)
stages.detail: Communalism three stages framework. Liberal → Extreme after 1937. Muslim League revival by Jinnah 1936. League 1937 poor performance (4.8% Muslim vote) → shift to mass communal politics. Hindu Mahasabha under Savarkar 1937-42 (Hindutva, 1923 text). RSS founded Vijayadashami 1925 by K.B. Hedgewar Nagpur. M.S. Golwalkar took over 1940 — "We, or Our Nationhood Defined" (1939). Iqbal's Allahabad Address Dec 1930. Rahmat Ali's "Pakistan" acronym 1933. Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution 23 March 1940 (moved by Fazlul Huq). Two-Nation Theory. Jinnah's 14 Points, "Caste Hindu Fascist Congress" rhetoric. Muslim Mass Contact Programme 1937 (Nehru). Unionist Party Punjab. Direct Action Day call 29 July 1946 → Calcutta Killings Aug 1946 → Noakhali, Bihar, Punjab, UP violence 1946-47. Gandhi's assassination 30 Jan 1948.

stages.label: Nationalist Foreign Policy (1920-47)
stages.detail: Roots 1878-1914: opposition to Afghan War 1878, Egypt 1882, Burma annexation 1885, Tibet 1903, NWF "forward policy". INC 1920 support for Turkey, 1921 Burma independence. Brussels Congress Feb 1927 — League Against Imperialism (Nehru elected to Exec Council, with Einstein, Rolland, Madame Sun Yat-Sen, Lansbury). Congress Foreign Department 1927. Madras 1927 + Calcutta 1928: support for Egypt, Syria, Palestine, Iraq, Afghanistan. 1936 active phase: Ethiopia Day May 9, Palestine Day Sept 27. Spanish Civil War support — Nehru+Krishna Menon visit Republican Spain June 1938. Haripura Congress Feb 1938 anti-Japan resolution. China Day June 12 1938. Medical mission to China (Dr M. Atal, Dr Dwarkanath Kotnis). Czechoslovakia/Munich Sept 1938 condemnation. Pro-Soviet sentiment (Nehru 1927 visit), concern for China and USSR during WWII.

stages.label: Visual Arts + Bengal School (1907-47)
stages.detail: Bengal School of Art: Abanindranath Tagore's "Bharat Mata" 1905 (era-8 tail), taught Nandalal Bose + Jamini Roy at Govt College of Art. Indian Society of Oriental Art 1907 (era 8). Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan 1919. Visva-Bharati University 1921. Nandalal Bose principal of Kala Bhavan 1922-51; painted Haripura Panels 1938; designed Constitution manuscript illustrations. Jamini Roy — Bengal folk + Kalighat-inspired modernism. Santiniketan as pan-Indian cultural centre. Asit Kumar Haldar, Kshitindranath Majumdar, Mukul Dey. Zainul Abedin's Bengal famine sketches 1943-44.

stages.label: Literature — Chhayavad + PWA (1918-47)
stages.detail: Chhayavad Movement 1918-1937 in Hindi poetry — four pillars: Jaishankar Prasad (Kamayani 1936), Suryakant Tripathi Nirala (Ram ki Shakti Puja), Sumitranandan Pant, Mahadevi Verma (Yama). Harivansh Rai Bachchan's Madhushala 1935. Premchand's Godan 1936 — already in ws. Urdu: Iqbal (Allahabad Address 1930), Faiz Ahmad Faiz (PWA), Saadat Hasan Manto, Ismat Chughtai (Lihaaf 1942 obscenity trial). Kazi Nazrul Islam — Bidrohi 1922 + Langal 1925 + Workers-Peasants Party. All India Progressive Writers' Association April 1936 Lucknow (President Premchand; founders Mulk Raj Anand, Sajjad Zaheer, Ahmed Ali). Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi's Saraswati magazine.

stages.label: Cinema + Theatre (1920-47)
stages.detail: Silent era through 1930: V. Shantaram, Baburao Painter, Suchet Singh, Madan, Ardeshir Irani. Alam Ara 14 March 1931 at Majestic Bombay — first Indian talkie (Imperial, Ardeshir Irani). Prabhat Film Company 1929 — Sairandhri 1933 first colour film, Sant Tukaram 1937 Venice. New Theatres Calcutta 1931 — P.C. Barua's Devdas 1935 first studio-system film. Bombay Talkies 1934 (Himansu Rai + Devika Rani) — Achhut Kanya 1936. IPTA 25 May 1943 Bombay — Bijon Bhattacharya's Nabanna on Bengal Famine, Dharti Ke Lal 1946 (K.A. Abbas). Prithvi Theatre 1944 (Prithviraj Kapoor). Kisan Kanya 1937 first indigenous colour. All India Radio. Early stars: Devika Rani, K.L. Saigal, Prithviraj Kapoor.

stages.label: Temporal Polity — Constitutional Scaffolding (1919-49)
stages.detail: NEW STREAM (per architecture decision). GoI Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — Dyarchy + bicameralism + Council of State + Legislative Assembly. Central PSC 1926. GoI Act 1935 — Federation, Three Lists, Provincial Autonomy, Federal Court 1937, RBI 1935. Communal Award Aug 1932 → Poona Pact Sept 1932. August Offer 1940 accepting CA demand. Cripps Proposals 1942 + opt-out. Cabinet Mission Plan three-tier federation May 1946. Indian Independence Act 18 July 1947. CA composition, major committees (8), Drafting Committee 7 members, B.N. Rau, Objectives Resolution, draft readings, 26 Nov 1949 adoption. Constitutional scaffolding running parallel to the mass-movement stream.

stages.label: Parallel — Europe, Fascism & WWII (1919-45)
stages.detail: Treaty of Sèvres May 1920 → Khilafat trigger. Weimar Germany, German Hyperinflation 1923. Nazi Party, Hitler Chancellor 1933, Enabling Act 1933, Nazi Racial Ideology, Gestapo+SS, Nuremberg Laws 1935. Great Depression 1929-1939. Holocaust begins 1941. World War II Europe Sept 1939-1945. Munich Agreement Sept 1938. Bretton Woods Conference 1944.

stages.label: Parallel — Soviet Stalinism (1922-45)
stages.detail: Formation of USSR 1922. Stalin's rise late 1920s, Collectivisation 1929, Five Year Plans 1927 onwards. Great Purge 1930s. WWII Eastern Front 1941-45 (Nazi attack on USSR 22 June 1941 — triggered CPI's "People's War" shift from Dec 1941).

stages.label: Parallel — Asian Anti-Colonial Nationalism (1919-47)
stages.detail: China: Long March 1934-35, Japanese Invasion 1937-45 (China Day June 12 in India). Japan: Pearl Harbor Dec 1941, overrun of SE Asia 1942, Rangoon fallen March 1942. Vietnam: Hoa Hao 1939, Ho Chi Minh + Viet Minh 1941, Vietnamese Independence Sept 1945. Indonesia: Sukarno, independence 1945. Bandung emergence.

nodes.label: Constituent Assembly
nodes.detail: Body that drafted the Indian Constitution. Formed in 1946 under Cabinet Mission Plan. Had 299 members. Worked from Dec 9, 1946 to Nov 26, 1949. Chaired by Dr Rajendra Prasad. Drafting Committee chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar.

nodes.label: Objective Resolution
nodes.detail: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. Laid down the philosophy and guiding principles for constitution-making. Later became the basis of the Preamble. Declared India to be an independent sovereign republic with guaranteed fundamental rights.

nodes.label: Drafting Committee
nodes.detail: Seven-member committee chaired by Ambedkar tasked with preparing the draft constitution. Other members included Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari.

nodes.label: Cabinet Mission Plan
nodes.detail: 1946 British mission that proposed the framework for forming the Constituent Assembly. Members elected by provincial legislatures through indirect election. Also proposed a three-tier federal structure which was eventually rejected.

nodes.label: Gandhi on Decentralisation
nodes.detail: Gandhi strongly pleaded for decentralisation of economic and political power. He envisioned every village as a republic, self-sustained and capable of managing its affairs. His concept of Gram Swaraj saw local self-governance as the foundation of democracy. Life would be a pyramid with apex sustained by the bottom. Influenced the creation of Panchayati Raj institutions.

nodes.label: Motilal Nehru Report (1928)
nodes.detail: Reaffirmed the conception of Indian citizenship and universal franchise. Declared that every person of either sex who has attained the age of twenty-one is entitled to vote. Showed that universal franchise was integral to Indian nationalism long before independence. Influential precursor to constitutional provisions on citizenship and voting rights.

nodes.label: League of Nations
nodes.detail: International organisation created after WWI to prevent war. Despite initial success, it failed to prevent WWII. The UN was founded as its successor in 1945 with lessons learned from its failure.

nodes.label: Refugee Crisis of 1947
nodes.detail: Partition caused massive displacement with about 80 lakh people migrating across borders. Refugees faced violence, abductions of women, separation of families. Rehabilitation of refugees was a major challenge for the new government.

nodes.label: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
nodes.detail: Known as Frontier Gandhi, undisputed leader of NWFP. Staunchly opposed the two-nation theory but his voice was ignored and NWFP was merged with Pakistan.

nodes.label: V.P. Menon
nodes.detail: Secretary in the Ministry of States under Sardar Patel. Played a crucial role in administrative and diplomatic negotiations for the integration of princely states. Drafted the Instrument of Accession.

nodes.label: Bombay Plan (1944)
nodes.detail: A joint proposal drafted by a section of big industrialists in 1944 for setting up a planned economy. Wanted the state to take major initiatives in industrial and economic investments. Significant because even private industrialists supported state-led planning.

nodes.label: Akali Dal
nodes.detail: Political wing of the Sikhs, formed in 1920. Led the movement for Punjabi Suba (achieved in 1966). Came to power in 1967 and 1977 in coalitions. The Anandpur Sahib Resolution of 1973 was its key political document. Fragmented during militancy period. Alliance with BJP won in 1997.

nodes.label: Karachi Session Resolution (1931)
nodes.detail: Indian National Congress resolution at Karachi session outlined how independent India's constitution should look. Committed to universal adult franchise, fundamental rights, and protection of minorities. Shaped the eventual Constituent Assembly deliberations.

nodes.label: Economic Impact of Partition
nodes.detail: India's partition in 1947 adversely affected agriculture as highly irrigated and fertile land went to Pakistan. India's jute industry suffered severely since almost all jute-producing areas became East Pakistan (now Bangladesh). India had enjoyed world monopoly in jute goods.
nodes.chapter_title: Indian Economy on the Eve of Independence

nodes.label: Ho Chi Minh
nodes.detail: Vietnamese communist leader who founded Viet Minh (Vietnam Doc Lap Dong Minh Hoi) in 1941. Inspired by Russian and Chinese revolutions. Declared Vietnam independent in 1945. Led resistance against French and Americans.

nodes.label: Vietnamese Independence
nodes.detail: Vietnam gained formal independence in 1945 but faced decades of fighting. French defeated at Dien Bien Phu 1954. Country divided at 17th parallel. NLF (Vietcong) fought US-backed South Vietnam. Reunified 1975.

nodes.label: Hoa Hao Movement
nodes.detail: Religious movement founded by Huynh Phu So in 1939 drawing on Buddhist traditions. Opposed French colonialism, rejected needless spending and promoted social reforms. French tried to suppress it by declaring So mad.

nodes.label: Non-Cooperation Movement (Detailed)
nodes.detail: Launched 1920 uniting Khilafat and Swaraj demands. Involved surrender of titles, boycott of councils, courts, schools. Foreign cloth imports halved 1920-22. Suspended after Chauri Chaura Feb 1922 where 22 policemen killed.

nodes.label: Civil Disobedience Movement
nodes.detail: Began with Salt March 1930. People broke salt law, picketed liquor and cloth shops, refused to pay revenue. Government responded with ordinances, arrests of 100,000. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931 led to suspension.

nodes.label: Khilafat Movement
nodes.detail: Led by Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali brothers after British imposed harsh treaty on Turkish Sultan (Khalifa) in 1920. Gandhi supported it for Hindu-Muslim unity. Merged with Non-Cooperation Movement.

nodes.label: Simon Commission
nodes.detail: British Commission of 1927 with no Indian member sent to decide India's political future. Met with protests across India with banners saying 'Simon Go Back'. Lala Lajpat Rai died from injuries during anti-Simon protest.

nodes.label: Gandhi-Irwin Pact
nodes.detail: Signed in March 1931 between Gandhi and Viceroy Irwin. Government agreed to release political prisoners. Gandhi agreed to participate in Round Table Conference in London. Civil Disobedience suspended.

nodes.label: Round Table Conferences
nodes.detail: Three conferences held in London (1930-32) to discuss constitutional reforms. First boycotted by Congress. Gandhi attended second but returned disappointed. Led to Government of India Act 1935.

nodes.label: Alluri Sitarama Raju
nodes.detail: Led militant guerrilla movement of tribal people in Andhra against colonial forest policies during 1920s. Claimed Gandhi had authorised use of force. Killed by British in 1924.

nodes.label: Women in Salt Satyagraha
nodes.detail: Thousands of women participated in Civil Disobedience, picketing liquor and foreign cloth shops. Initially Gandhi opposed women's participation until Sarojini Naidu persuaded him. Women became integral to national movement.

nodes.label: Depressed Classes and National Movement
nodes.detail: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for dalits at Round Table Conference. Gandhi opposed this leading to Poona Pact 1932 with reserved seats within joint electorates. Tension between Congress and dalit leadership.

nodes.label: Poona Pact 1932
nodes.detail: Agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar replacing separate electorates for dalits with reserved seats within general electorate. Gandhi undertook fast unto death against separate electorates. Shaped future reservation policy.

nodes.label: Great Depression
nodes.detail: 1929 Wall Street crash caused worldwide economic crisis. US lending stopped, prices fell, factories closed. India's agricultural exports and food prices crashed, devastating peasants while British continued to collect revenue.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of a Global World

nodes.label: Bretton Woods System
nodes.detail: 1944 conference established IMF and World Bank for post-war economic stability. Fixed exchange rates pegged to US dollar anchored to gold. Decision-making controlled by Western powers. Collapsed in 1970s.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of a Global World

nodes.label: Premchand's Novels
nodes.detail: Munshi Premchand wrote about Indian peasant life, caste oppression, and colonial exploitation. Godan (1936) depicted tragedy of peasant Hori. Rangbhoomi explored social conflicts. Brought Hindi novel to literary maturity.

nodes.label: Long March (1934-35)
nodes.detail: Epic retreat of the Chinese Communist Red Army over 9,000 km from Jiangxi to Shaanxi province to escape Nationalist encirclement. Of about 100,000 who started, only 8,000-10,000 survived. Mao emerged as the undisputed CCP leader during the march. Became a founding myth of the People's Republic.

nodes.label: John Marshall
nodes.detail: Director-General of ASI who announced the discovery of a new Indus Valley Civilisation to the world in 1924. First professional archaeologist to work in India. Made India 'three thousand years older'. However, his horizontal excavation method ignored stratigraphy.
nodes.chapter_title: Bricks, Beads and Bones - The Harappan Civilisation

nodes.label: R.E.M. Wheeler
nodes.detail: Director-General of ASI from 1944. Introduced stratigraphic excavation methods to Indian archaeology, rectifying Marshall's approach. Excavated at Harappa in 1946. Initially proposed Aryan invasion theory for Harappan decline based on skeletal evidence, later challenged.
nodes.chapter_title: Bricks, Beads and Bones - The Harappan Civilisation

nodes.label: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
nodes.detail: Launched by Gandhi in 1920 against Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Indians boycotted councils, courts, schools, foreign cloth. Tilak Swaraj Fund raised Rs 1 crore. Suspended after Chauri Chaura violence (February 1922) where 22 policemen were killed by mob.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Salt March / Dandi March (1930)
nodes.detail: Gandhi marched 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi (12 March - 6 April 1930) to break salt law. Launched Civil Disobedience Movement. Brilliantly chosen issue as salt tax affected every Indian. International media coverage. Led to Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and Round Table Conference.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Quit India Movement (1942)
nodes.detail: Launched 8 August 1942 with Gandhi's call 'Do or Die'. Demanded immediate British withdrawal from India. All Congress leaders arrested immediately. Spontaneous mass protests, strikes, sabotage across India. Severely repressed by British. Demonstrated depth of popular support for independence.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34)
nodes.detail: Began with Salt March. Indians broke salt laws, boycotted foreign goods, refused to pay taxes. Massive participation including women. Over 60,000 arrested. Suspended for Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Resumed 1932 after Second Round Table Conference failed. Formally withdrawn 1934.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Chauri Chaura Incident (1922)
nodes.detail: Violent mob killed 22 policemen at Chauri Chaura (UP) on 5 February 1922. Gandhi immediately suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement, insisting on non-violence. Decision shocked many Congress leaders but showed Gandhi's uncompromising commitment to ahimsa.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Cripps Mission (1942)
nodes.detail: Sir Stafford Cripps sent to India in March 1942 offering dominion status after war, with right of provinces to opt out. Congress rejected as too little too late. Muslim League found opt-out clause interesting for Pakistan demand. Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: INA Trials (1945)
nodes.detail: British put Indian National Army officers on trial at Red Fort, Delhi. INA was formed by Subhas Chandra Bose with Japanese support. Trials united Indian public opinion against British. Congress defended INA soldiers. Demonstrated that Indian armed forces could no longer be relied upon by British.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Government of India Act 1935
nodes.detail: Major constitutional legislation providing for provincial autonomy, federal structure, and separate electorates. Congress won majority in 1937 elections in most provinces. Formed governments in 8 of 11 provinces. Muslim League performed poorly outside Muslim-majority areas. Framework for 1946 elections.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Lahore Congress Session (1929)
nodes.detail: Congress session under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as goal on 31 December 1929. 26 January 1930 celebrated as first Independence Day. Authorised Gandhi to launch Civil Disobedience Movement.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (1946)
nodes.detail: Mutiny by Indian sailors of Royal Indian Navy in Bombay (February 1946) against racial discrimination and poor conditions. Spread to other naval establishments. Demonstrated that Indian armed forces were unreliable for British. Along with INA trials, hastened British decision to leave India.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Partition of India (1947)
nodes.detail: Division of British India into India and Pakistan on 14-15 August 1947. Largest mass migration in history: 15 million displaced, estimated 1 million killed. Punjab and Bengal divided. Accompanied by horrific communal violence. Radcliffe Line drawn hastily as boundary.

nodes.label: Lahore Resolution (1940)
nodes.detail: Muslim League resolution demanding autonomous and sovereign Muslim-majority areas in northwestern and eastern India. Did not use the word 'Pakistan' explicitly. Became basis for demand for separate Muslim state. Sometimes called Pakistan Resolution.

nodes.label: Two-Nation Theory
nodes.detail: Theory that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations with distinct histories, cultures and social systems. Used by Jinnah and Muslim League to justify demand for Pakistan. Challenged by Congress and secular nationalists. Savarkar and some Hindu Mahasabha members also endorsed Hindu nationalism.

nodes.label: Cabinet Mission (1946)
nodes.detail: British mission proposing federal structure with three groups of provinces (Hindu-majority, Muslim-majority NW, Muslim-majority East) sharing centre for defence, foreign affairs and communications. Both Congress and League initially accepted but later disagreed on interpretation, leading to its failure.

nodes.label: Direct Action Day (16 August 1946)
nodes.detail: Called by Muslim League after withdrawing acceptance of Cabinet Mission Plan. Led to massive communal riots in Calcutta ('Great Calcutta Killing') with over 4,000 dead. Violence spread to Noakhali, Bihar and elsewhere. Demonstrated that communal peace could not be maintained.

nodes.label: Mountbatten Plan (June 1947)
nodes.detail: Lord Mountbatten, last Viceroy, advanced independence date to August 1947 from June 1948. Plan for partition accepted by Congress (reluctantly), Muslim League and Sikhs. Radcliffe Boundary Commission appointed to draw borders. Princely states given choice to join India or Pakistan.

nodes.label: Radcliffe Line
nodes.detail: Boundary between India and Pakistan drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe who had never visited India. Drawn in just 5 weeks, dividing Punjab and Bengal. Announced on 17 August 1947, two days after independence. Affected millions who found themselves on the wrong side.

nodes.label: Communal Violence During Partition
nodes.detail: Horrific violence in Punjab, Bengal, Delhi and elsewhere. Massacres, abductions of women, forced conversions, destruction of property. Trains carrying refugees arrived with dead bodies. Women sometimes killed by their own families to prevent 'dishonour'. Gandhi fasted to stop Delhi violence.

nodes.label: 1946 Elections
nodes.detail: Crucial elections held under Government of India Act 1935. Congress swept general seats. Muslim League won every Muslim seat in Central Assembly and most in provinces, validating its claim to represent Muslims. Demonstrated communal polarisation. Formed basis for partition demand.

nodes.label: Noakhali Riots (1946)
nodes.detail: Communal violence in Noakhali (Bengal) in October 1946 targeting Hindu minority. Gandhi walked through Noakhali villages for months promoting communal harmony. Retaliatory violence against Muslims in Bihar. These events deepened communal divide and made partition seem inevitable.

nodes.label: Interim Government (1946)
nodes.detail: Formed September 1946 under Nehru as Vice President of Viceroy's Executive Council. Muslim League joined in October but obstructed functioning. Deadlock between Congress and League in interim government convinced many that partition was unavoidable.

nodes.label: Gandhi's Opposition to Partition
nodes.detail: Gandhi opposed partition till the very end, calling it 'vivisection of India'. Fasted in Calcutta (August-September 1947) to stop communal violence. Fasted in Delhi (January 1948) to protect Muslims and ensure payment of Rs 55 crore to Pakistan. Assassinated partly for these stances.

nodes.label: Constituent Assembly
nodes.detail: Elected in July 1946 under Cabinet Mission plan. 296 members for British India, reduced after partition. First meeting 9 December 1946. Drafting Committee under Ambedkar appointed 29 August 1947. Completed work on 26 November 1949. Constitution came into effect 26 January 1950.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Objectives Resolution
nodes.detail: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946. Declared India a sovereign democratic republic guaranteeing justice, equality, freedom. Adequate safeguards for minorities. Became Preamble of the Constitution. Debated extensively by members from all communities.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Drafting Committee
nodes.detail: Seven-member committee appointed 29 August 1947 under Ambedkar's chairmanship. Other members: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau (replaced B.L. Mitter), T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan).
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Integration of Princely States
nodes.detail: 562 princely states had to decide between India and Pakistan. Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon convinced most to accede to India. Hyderabad integrated through Operation Polo (1948). Junagadh through plebiscite. Kashmir's accession triggered Indo-Pak conflict. Completed by 1949.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Government of India Act 1935 (as template)
nodes.detail: About 250 clauses of the Constitution were adapted from the 1935 Act. Provided administrative framework including federal structure, provincial governance, public service commissions. Critics called it overly influenced by colonial legislation, but framers argued practical continuity was essential.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Khadi and Nationalism
nodes.detail: During the national movement, Mahatma Gandhi urged boycott of imported textiles and use of hand-spun hand-woven cloth. Khadi became a symbol of nationalism and the charkha was placed at the centre of the Congress tricolour in 1931.
nodes.chapter_title: Weavers, Iron Smelters and Factory Owners

nodes.label: Gandhi on Education
nodes.detail: Gandhi argued colonial education created inferiority complex, enslaved Indians, and made them strangers in their own land. Advocated education in Indian languages with focus on handicrafts, practical knowledge and all-round development of body, mind and spirit.
nodes.chapter_title: Civilising the Native, Educating the Nation

nodes.label: B.R. Ambedkar
nodes.detail: Born into Mahar family, experienced caste prejudice in school. Studied in US, wrote extensively on upper-caste power. Started temple entry movement in 1927. Led Dalit movement for social equality and became Chairman of Constitution's Drafting Committee.

nodes.label: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar)
nodes.detail: Founded Self Respect Movement. Argued untouchables upheld original Tamil and Dravidian culture subjugated by Brahmans. Criticized Hindu scriptures including Manu's codes and Ramayana for establishing Brahman authority.

nodes.label: Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929
nodes.detail: Passed in 1929 without bitter debates. Set minimum marriage age at 18 for men and 16 for women. Subsequently raised to 21 for men and 18 for women.

nodes.label: Salt March / Dandi March
nodes.detail: In 1930 Gandhi marched 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi to break salt law. Related freedom to a specific grievance shared by all. Thousands arrested. Led to Civil Disobedience Movement with mass participation.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of the National Movement: 1870s-1947

nodes.label: Quit India Movement
nodes.detail: Launched August 1942 with Gandhi's 'do or die' call. Leaders jailed immediately but movement spread. By end of 1943, over 90,000 arrested, around 1,000 killed. People set up their own governments in many areas.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of the National Movement: 1870s-1947

nodes.label: Bhagat Singh
nodes.detail: Revolutionary nationalist who founded HSRA in 1928. Assassinated officer Saunders in 1928 for Lajpat Rai's death. Threw bomb in Central Legislative Assembly in 1929. Executed on 23 March 1931 at age 23.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of the National Movement: 1870s-1947

nodes.label: Subhas Chandra Bose and INA
nodes.detail: Radical nationalist with socialist leanings. Secretly left India in 1941, went to Singapore via Germany. Raised Azad Hind Fauj (INA). Attempted to enter India through Imphal-Kohima in 1944 but campaign failed.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of the National Movement: 1870s-1947

nodes.label: Purna Swaraj Resolution 1929
nodes.detail: Congress resolved to fight for complete independence in 1929 under presidentship of Jawaharlal Nehru. Independence Day observed on 26 January 1930 all over the country.
nodes.chapter_title: The Making of the National Movement: 1870s-1947

nodes.label: Stalin's Collectivisation
nodes.detail: From 1929 Stalin forced peasants into collective farms (kolkhoz). 'Kulaks' eliminated, land and implements transferred to collectives. Peasants resisted, destroyed livestock. Bad harvests 1930-33 caused famine killing over 4 million.
nodes.chapter_title: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

nodes.label: Five Year Plans (USSR)
nodes.detail: Centralised planning with government-set targets for five-year periods. First two plans (1927-38) led to 100% increase in oil, coal and steel production. New factory cities built but with poor working conditions.
nodes.chapter_title: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

nodes.label: Formation of USSR
nodes.detail: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics created from Russian empire in December 1922. Non-Russian nationalities given political autonomy. Became one-party state with trade unions under party control and secret police (Cheka/OGPU/NKVD).
nodes.chapter_title: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution

nodes.label: Adolf Hitler
nodes.detail: Born 1889 in Austria. Joined German Workers Party in 1919, renamed it Nazi Party. Became Chancellor in 1933. Established dictatorship through Enabling Act. Pursued racial ideology and territorial expansion. Committed suicide April 1945.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Nazi Party
nodes.detail: National Socialist German Workers' Party renamed from German Workers' Party by Hitler. Got 2.6% votes in 1928 but became largest party with 37% by 1932 during Great Depression. Used propaganda, rallies and spectacle.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Enabling Act 1933
nodes.detail: Passed 3 March 1933, established dictatorship by giving Hitler power to sideline Parliament and rule by decree. All parties and trade unions banned except Nazi Party. State controlled economy, media, army and judiciary.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: The Holocaust
nodes.detail: Systematic murder of 6 million Jews, 200,000 Gypsies, 1 million Polish civilians, 70,000 disabled Germans. Gas chambers at Auschwitz, Treblinka, and other death camps in Poland. Nuremberg Tribunal sentenced 11 Nazi leaders to death.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Nuremberg Laws 1935
nodes.detail: Laws denying citizenship to Jews, forbidding Jewish-German marriages, confiscating Jewish property. Led to three stages: Exclusion (1933-39), Ghettoisation (1940-44), and Annihilation (1941 onwards).
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Great Depression
nodes.detail: Started with Wall Street crash on 24 October 1929 when 13 million shares sold in one day. US national income halved. Germany worst hit: industrial production fell to 40% of 1929 level, 6 million unemployed.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: German Hyperinflation 1923
nodes.detail: When Germany refused to pay reparations, France occupied Ruhr. Germany printed money recklessly. Dollar went from 24,000 marks in April to trillions in December. Germans carried cartloads of currency for bread.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Nazi Racial Ideology
nodes.detail: Racial hierarchy placing Nordic German Aryans at top and Jews at bottom. Drew from Darwin and Herbert Spencer's survival of fittest. Lebensraum (living space) concept demanded eastward territorial expansion.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Gestapo and SS
nodes.detail: Gestapo (secret state police), SS (protection squads), criminal police and Security Service (SD) created to control society. Extra-constitutional powers to detain, torture, deport without legal procedures.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: World War II in Europe
nodes.detail: Germany invaded Poland September 1939 starting WWII. Tripartite Pact with Italy and Japan 1940. Invaded USSR June 1941. Defeated at Stalingrad. War ended May 1945 with Hitler's suicide and Allied victory.
nodes.chapter_title: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler

nodes.label: Dust Bowl of 1930s
nodes.detail: Terrifying black blizzards of dust in US Great Plains in 1930s. Over-ploughing had destroyed topsoil. Drought worsened conditions. By 1930s, over 38 million acres grassland ploughed recklessly for wheat.

nodes.label: Pentangular Tournament
nodes.detail: Cricket tournament in Bombay with five teams based on community: Europeans, Parsees, Hindus, Muslims and The Rest. Gandhi and nationalists criticised it for dividing Indians along communal lines. Replaced by Ranji Trophy.
nodes.chapter_title: History and Sport: The Story of Cricket

nodes.label: Board of Control for Cricket in India
nodes.detail: Established in 1928 to administer cricket in India. By late 20th century became the richest cricket board in the world due to India's massive television audience and commercial potential of the sport.
nodes.chapter_title: History and Sport: The Story of Cricket

nodes.label: Swadeshi and Clothing Politics
nodes.detail: During national movement, Indian clothing became political. Gandhi adopted short dhoti and chaddar, rejecting Western dress. Swadeshi movement advocated burning of imported cloth and wearing khadi as political statement.

nodes.label: Gandhi's Clothing Politics
nodes.detail: Gandhi deliberately adopted the dress of the poorest Indian - short dhoti, chaddar, no shoes. This was a political statement about identifying with the masses and rejecting British sartorial standards. Charkha became national symbol.

nodes.label: Subhas Chandra Bose
nodes.detail: Radical nationalist who disagreed with Gandhi's methods. Elected Congress President 1938-39 but forced to resign. Escaped to Germany (1941), then to Japan. Founded Azad Hind Fauj (INA) and Azad Hind government. Gave call 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'. Died 1945.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
nodes.detail: Leader of Muslim League, called Quaid-e-Azam. Initially an ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity in Congress. Grew disillusioned with Congress, especially after 1937 provincial governments. Advocated Two-Nation Theory. Demanded Pakistan from 1940 Lahore Resolution. Became first Governor-General of Pakistan.

nodes.label: Jawaharlal Nehru
nodes.detail: First Prime Minister of independent India. Congress president during Lahore session (1929). Led Congress negotiations during Cabinet Mission and partition. Reluctantly accepted partition to avoid civil war. Delivered 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on 14 August 1947.

nodes.label: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
nodes.detail: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India. Integrated 562 princely states into Indian Union. Early advocate of accepting partition to consolidate India. Organised mass integration of princely states including Hyderabad, Junagadh and Kashmir through diplomacy and force.

nodes.label: Lord Mountbatten
nodes.detail: Last Viceroy of India (March-August 1947), then first Governor-General of independent India. Accelerated partition timeline. Worked closely with Nehru. Appointed Radcliffe Boundary Commission. His hasty decisions are debated for contributing to partition violence.

nodes.label: B.R. Ambedkar
nodes.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Dalit leader and constitutional scholar, studied at Columbia and London. Argued for abolishing caste and ensuring fundamental rights for depressed classes. Key architect of provisions on equality, untouchability abolition and reservation.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Rajendra Prasad
nodes.detail: President of the Constituent Assembly. Later became first President of India (1950-1962). Lawyer from Bihar who participated in Champaran Satyagraha. Presided over Assembly deliberations and signed the completed Constitution on 24 January 1950.
nodes.chapter_title: Framing the Constitution - The Beginning of a New Era

nodes.label: Mahatma Gandhi
nodes.detail: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (1869-1948). Returned from South Africa to India in 1915. Transformed the nationalist movement through satyagraha (truth-force), ahimsa (non-violence) and mass mobilisation. Called 'Mahatma' by Rabindranath Tagore. Assassinated 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse.
nodes.chapter_title: Mahatma Gandhi and the Nationalist Movement - Civil Disobedience and Beyond

nodes.label: Treaty of Sèvres (May 1920)
nodes.detail: May 1920 treaty with Ottoman Turkey that formalised dismemberment of the Turkish/Ottoman Empire. Signed after WWI, it convinced Indian Muslims that British promises to preserve the Caliphate had been broken, pushing the Khilafat Committee to adopt Gandhi's non-cooperation programme on 9 June 1920 at Allahabad.

nodes.label: Hunter Committee (1919-20)
nodes.detail: Official British inquiry into Jallianwala Bagh and Punjab disturbances. Widely seen as a whitewash — minor criticism of Dyer but effectively exonerated British officials. The House of Lords voted in favour of Dyer and Morning Post raised 30,000 pounds for him, outraging Indian opinion and pushing Congress toward Non-Cooperation.

nodes.label: Calcutta Special Session (Sept 1920)
nodes.detail: Special session of INC held September 1920. Adopted Non-Cooperation Movement despite opposition led by C.R. Das to boycott of legislative councils. First major Congress endorsement of Gandhian extra-constitutional methods.

nodes.label: Nagpur Session (Dec 1920)
nodes.detail: Annual INC session December 1920. C.R. Das moved the main resolution on Non-Cooperation. Congress creed changed from "self-government by constitutional and legal means" to "Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means". New Congress constitution (Gandhi's drafting) introduced Working Committee of 15, PCCs on linguistic basis, membership reduced to 4 annas, village/mohalla committees, Hindi as working language.

nodes.label: Ali Brothers (Mohammed Ali & Shaukat Ali)
nodes.detail: Mohammed Ali and Shaukat Ali — foremost Khilafat leaders. Travelled nationwide with Gandhi during Non-Cooperation. Mohammed Ali's July 1921 Karachi declaration that it was "religiously unlawful for Muslims to serve in British Army" led to his arrest and the famous 4 October 1921 manifesto by 47 Congressmen.

nodes.label: Tilak Swaraj Fund (1921)
nodes.detail: Fund launched by Congress at Vijayawada AICC (April 1921). Target of Rs 1 crore was oversubscribed. Used for national schools, charkha distribution, and Congress organisation. Symbol of mass popular support for NCM — Congress membership reached ~50 lakhs.

nodes.label: Congress Volunteer Corps (1921)
nodes.detail: Uniformed parallel "people's police" that grew during Non-Cooperation. Marched in formation, organised protests, enforced boycott. Declared illegal by government in December 1921; arrests of Corps members triggered wave of Congress leader arrests (~30,000 in 2 months).

nodes.label: Prince of Wales Visit (Nov 1921)
nodes.detail: 17 November 1921 — Prince of Wales landed in Bombay to empty streets and hartal. Clashes between welcome-party attendees and boycott crowd returning from Gandhi's meeting led to three-day riots in Bombay; 59 dead. Parsis, Christians, Anglo-Indians targeted as loyalists. Gandhi fasted 3 days. Disturbed Gandhi about mass violence risk.

nodes.label: Ahmedabad Session (Dec 1921)
nodes.detail: Annual INC session Dec 1921. Appointed Gandhi as sole authority on mass civil disobedience. Under pressure from rank-and-file to escalate, Gandhi announced Bardoli as site of CD but withdrew after Chauri-Chaura.

nodes.label: C.R. Das (Chittaranjan Das)
nodes.detail: Deshbandhu (1870-1925). Bengali nationalist, lawyer. Initially opposed legislative-council boycott at Calcutta 1920 but moved the Non-Cooperation resolution at Nagpur Dec 1920 after voter turnout collapsed. Arrested Dec 1921 along with his wife Basanti Debi. Later co-founded Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru (1923). Died June 1925.

nodes.label: Oudh Kisan Sabha (Oct 1920)
nodes.detail: Non-Cooperator alternative to UP Kisan Sabha, founded 17 October 1920 at Pratapgarh. Integrated 330+ village kisan sabhas across Avadh. Founded by Gauri Shankar Misra, Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra, Mata Badal Pande, Deo Narayan Pande, Kedar Nath. Demands: refuse to till bedakhli land, no hari/begar forced labour, solve disputes via panchayats. Ayodhya rally of 100,000 peasants on 20-21 Dec 1920.

nodes.label: Baba Ramchandra
nodes.detail: Maharashtrian Brahmin sadhu who became rallying figure for Avadh peasant movement in mid-1920. Arrested 28 August 1920 on trumped-up theft charge; peasant mobilisation secured his release. Central to Oudh Kisan Sabha. At Ayodhya rally, appeared bound in ropes to symbolise kisan oppression.

nodes.label: Eka Movement (1921-22)
nodes.detail: Peasant "unity" movement in Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur (northern Avadh) late 1921. Grievances: rent 50% above record rates, thekedar oppression, share-rents. Ritual oaths taken around water-filled "Ganges" pit. Leadership passed to Madari Pasi and low-caste leaders who rejected non-violence discipline. Unlike Kisan Sabha, included small zamindars. Crushed by March 1922.

nodes.label: Moplah (Mappila) Rebellion (1921)
nodes.detail: August-December 1921 uprising of Muslim Mappila tenants in Malabar, Kerala. Initial impetus from Manjeri Conference April 1920 that supported tenants' cause. Merged with Khilafat movement. Triggered 20 Aug 1921 by raid on Tirurangadi mosque to arrest Ali Musaliar. Initial targets: Hindu landlords (jenmies), courts, police stations. After martial law, rebellion acquired communal character with forced conversions. Leaders: Ali Musaliar, Kunhammed Haji. Suppressed by Dec 1921: 2,337 dead officially, 45,404 captured. Drove wedge between Mappilas and NCM; political isolation lasted till independence.

nodes.label: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
nodes.detail: No-tax movement in Bardoli taluq, Surat district, Feb-Aug 1928. Triggered by 30% land-revenue reassessment recommended by Jayakar; Bardoli Inquiry Committee 1926 found it unjustified. Vallabhbhai Patel led — earned title "Sardar" from women of Bardoli. Organisation: 13 Chhavanis (workers' camps), 100 workers + 1,500 volunteers, Bardoli Satyagraha Patrika daily. Intelligence wing monitored waverers. Women (Mithuben Petit, Maniben Patel, others) and Kaliparaj tribal base mobilised. Governor Irwin pressured Bombay to retreat; Broomfield-Maxwell enquiry reduced enhancement to 6.03%. Massive win preceded CD 1930.

nodes.label: Kaliparaj → Raniparaj Uplift Work
nodes.detail: Bardoli Congress workers' social reform project among tribal "Kaliparaj" (dark people, 60% of taluq) from 1922. Ashram network (6 ashrams) taught literacy, exposed Hali hereditary-labour system. Kunverji Mehta and Keshavji Ganeshji developed "Kaliparaj literature". Gandhi renamed them "Raniparaj" (forest inhabitants) in 1927. Built base that later supported Bardoli Satyagraha against upper-caste landlord counter-mobilisation.

nodes.label: All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC)
nodes.detail: Founded 1920 as first all-India labour federation. Lala Lajpat Rai first president, Dewan Chaman Lal first General Secretary. Tilak was a moving spirit in its formation. Its manifesto urged workers to participate in nationalist politics: "political freedom is of no worth without economic freedom". C.R. Das presided over 3rd and 4th sessions. 1928 Jharia session saw Communist dominance; corporatist trend led by N.M. Joshi split away at the Nehru-presided subsequent session.

nodes.label: Dewan Chaman Lal
nodes.detail: First General Secretary of AITUC (1920). Major figure in Indian labour movement. Moved resolution at 2nd AITUC session declaring Swaraj must be "not for the capitalists but for the workers".

nodes.label: Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (TLA)
nodes.detail: Founded 1918 by Gandhi. 14,000 workers at peak — largest single trade union of its time. Built on Gandhi's trusteeship principle and arbitration (capitalist as trustee of workers' interests). Won 27.5% wage hike in 1918 dispute. Model of non-confrontational labour-capital relations that also retained radical potential (workers were "real masters" per Gandhi).

nodes.label: Workers' and Peasants' Parties (WPP)
nodes.detail: By early 1927, Communist groups organised as WPPs in different parts of India, functioning as left-wing within Congress. Leaders: S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, P.C. Joshi, Sohan Singh Josh. Gained strength in Congress provincial and all-India organisation. Dissolved after Meerut Conspiracy arrests 1929 and Communist shift away from united front.

nodes.label: S.A. Dange
nodes.detail: Shripad Amrit Dange. Early Communist leader, WPP figure, accused in Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33). Later General Secretary of CPI. Prolific trade unionist and writer.

nodes.label: Muzaffar Ahmed
nodes.detail: Founding member of Communist Party of India. WPP Bengal leader. Arrested in Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case (1924) and Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929). Senior figure in Bengal labour and peasant movements.

nodes.label: P.C. Joshi
nodes.detail: Puran Chand Joshi. Communist leader; later General Secretary of CPI (1935-47). Instrumental in CPI's decision to support WWII as "people's war" from 1941 (after Nazi attack on USSR) and to dissociate from Quit India 1942.

nodes.label: Girni Kamgar Union (1928)
nodes.detail: Communist-led Bombay textile union. Rose to pre-eminence after the historic six-month Bombay Textile Strike (April-September 1928). Membership jumped from 324 to 54,000 by Dec 1928. Fell to ~800 by end 1929 after Communist withdrawal from united national front.

nodes.label: Bombay Textile Strike (April-Sept 1928)
nodes.detail: Six-month general strike by Bombay textile workers, April-September 1928. Communist-led under Girni Kamgar Union. Historic scale — unified Bombay working class, cemented Communist influence in labour movement, and alarmed the colonial government into the repressive legislation (Public Safety Act, Trade Disputes Act) that followed.

nodes.label: Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33)
nodes.detail: Government prosecution launched March 1929 against 32 Communist, WPP, and trade union leaders on charges of conspiring to deprive the King of his sovereignty. Trial lasted four years. Made Communist leaders nationally famous; Nehru, Gandhi and others publicly defended the accused. Severely damaged organised left but generated sympathy for its cause. Key accused included S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, Philip Spratt, Ben Bradley.

nodes.label: Public Safety Act + Trade Disputes Act (1929)
nodes.detail: Twin 1929 laws passed by colonial government to crush organised labour. Trade Disputes Act restricted strike action in public utilities and made lightning strikes illegal. Public Safety Bill aimed at deporting foreign communists, dropped after Bhagat Singh-Batukeshwar Dutt bomb in Central Legislative Assembly 8 April 1929 protesting these bills.

nodes.label: Royal Commission on Labour (1929) — Whitley Commission
nodes.detail: Set up 1929 under J.H. Whitley. Dual-purpose move — concession to wean moderate labour from militant stream while Meerut Conspiracy Case crushed radicals. Report (1931) formed basis of later factories, industrial disputes and labour welfare legislation.

nodes.label: Sholapur Textile Workers Uprising (May 1930)
nodes.detail: 7-16 May 1930 — textile workers of Sholapur went on rampage after police fired on anti-British procession during Civil Disobedience Movement. Attacked government offices, courts, police stations, railway stations. Rebels held city for several days; national flag hoisted over town. Martial law imposed. Multiple workers hanged. One of the high points of CDM worker participation.

nodes.label: All India Post & Telegraph Strike (1946)
nodes.detail: Landmark nationwide strike 1946 by Post & Telegraph Department workers. Symbolic of post-war economic grievances (high prices, food scarcity, drop in real wages, post-war demobilisation) and pre-independence anticipation. Part of 1945-47 worker upsurge.

nodes.label: Akali Movement (1920-25)
nodes.detail: Sikh reform movement 1920-25 to free Gurdwaras from corrupt mahants who collaborated with British (e.g. Amritsar priests honoured General Dyer with saropa). >30,000 imprisoned, ~400 killed, 2,000+ wounded. SGPC formed Nov 1920; Shiromani Akali Dal formed Dec 1920 (political arm). Non-violent creed adopted under NCM influence. Jat peasantry backbone, nationalist intellectual leadership. Culminated in Sikh Gurdwaras Act July 1925.

nodes.label: Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee (SGPC)
nodes.detail: Central body elected by 10,000-strong Sikh assembly Nov 1920 — committee of 175 to manage Golden Temple, Akal Takht and other Gurdwaras. Became statutory elected body after Sikh Gurdwaras Act 1925. Passed May 1921 resolution for non-cooperation: boycott of foreign goods/liquor, panchayats instead of British courts.

nodes.label: Nankana Tragedy (Feb 1921)
nodes.detail: 20 February 1921 — at Nankana, birthplace of Guru Nanak, Mahant Narain Das's 500 mercenaries opened fire on peaceful Akali jatha entering the Gurdwara to pray. ~100 Akalis killed. Kartar Singh Jhabbar's jathas liberated the Gurdwara. Gandhi, Shaukat Ali, Lajpat Rai visited in solidarity. Turning point that integrated Akali movement with national struggle.

nodes.label: Keys Affair (Oct-Nov 1921)
nodes.detail: October 1921 — government attempt to keep possession of keys of Golden Temple Toshakhana triggered mass Akali protest. Baba Kharak Singh, Master Tara Singh arrested. Government climbed down, released all, surrendered keys to Baba Kharak Singh (SGPC head). Gandhi telegrammed: "First battle for India's freedom won. Congratulations." Major symbolic Akali victory.

nodes.label: Guru-Ka-Bagh Morcha (Aug-Sept 1922)
nodes.detail: 9 August 1922 onwards — Akali non-violent struggle at Guru-Ka-Bagh Gurdwara near Amritsar. Over 4,000 Akalis arrested for tree-cutting "theft". Police beatings (instead of arrests) on volunteers who refused to yield. C.F. Andrews called the oppression a "moral defeat of England". Climbed down when retired govt servant leased disputed land. National outrage, Congress investigation committee appointed.

nodes.label: Sikh Gurdwaras Act (July 1925)
nodes.detail: Legislation passed July 1925 — handed control over all Punjab Gurdwaras to an elected body of Sikhs (statutory SGPC). Culmination of Akali Movement 1920-25. Model of successful religious-reform movement that remained non-communal in its popular base.

nodes.label: Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25)
nodes.detail: Temple-entry Satyagraha at Vaikom, Travancore, begun 30 March 1924 — demanded right for avarnas (Ezhavas, Pulayas) to use temple roads. Led by K.P. Kesava Menon (Kerala Provincial Congress). Nationwide support: Akali jatha from Punjab, E.V. Ramaswami Naicker (Periyar) led jatha from Madurai (jailed). Savarna jatha of 1,000+ marched to Trivandrum Oct 1924. Maharani refused. Gandhi toured Kerala March 1925, negotiated compromise: outer temple roads opened to avarnas; inner Sankethan remained closed.

nodes.label: K.P. Kesava Menon
nodes.detail: Kerala Congress leader who led Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25). Co-founder of Mathrubhumi newspaper 1923. Major figure in Malabar Congress and Kerala anti-untouchability movement.

nodes.label: Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931-32)
nodes.detail: Temple-entry Satyagraha at Guruvayur, launched 1 November 1931 by KPCC. Led by K. Kelappan. Jatha of 16 volunteers led by poet Subramanian Tirumambu ("Singing Sword of Kerala") marched from Cannanore. A.K. Gopalan and P. Krishna Pillai (future Communist leaders) mercilessly beaten. Kelappan fasted unto death 21 Sept 1932; Gandhi intervened, Kelappan broke fast 2 October 1932. Temple opened only in 1947 but campaign thrived.

nodes.label: K. Kelappan
nodes.detail: Kerala Gandhian leader. Led Guruvayur temple-entry Satyagraha 1931-32. Fasted unto death 21 Sept 1932 demanding temple opening. Broke fast 2 October on Gandhi's intervention. Major figure in Kerala nationalist and anti-untouchability movements; later active in Bhoodan movement.

nodes.label: A.K. Gopalan
nodes.detail: Started as Gandhian, became Communist leader of Kerala. Beaten mercilessly at Guruvayur Satyagraha 1931. Led 1,000-mile Kerala jatha after Kelappan's fast. Later founded All India Kisan Sabha Kerala branch. First leader of Opposition in Indian Parliament 1952-54 (CPI).

nodes.label: Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (Nov 1936)
nodes.detail: 12 November 1936 — Maharaja of Travancore issued proclamation throwing open all government-controlled temples to all Hindus irrespective of caste. Landmark — first major princely/government implementation of temple entry for depressed classes. Result of sustained Kerala temple-entry agitation and Congress pressure.

nodes.label: Madras Temple Entry Act (1938)
nodes.detail: 1938 — Madras Congress Ministry headed by C. Rajagopalachari passed Temple Entry Authorisation Act. Other Congress-ruled provinces followed. Concrete achievement of Congress provincial rule 1937-39 for anti-untouchability movement.

nodes.label: Swaraj Party (Jan 1923)
nodes.detail: Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party, founded 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das (President) and Motilal Nehru (Secretary) after the Gaya Session defeated council-entry (1748 vs 890). Programme: contest elections, enter legislatures, wreck "sham reforms" from within via "uniform, continuous and consistent obstruction". Won 42/101 Central Legislative Assembly seats Nov 1923; majority in Central Provinces; largest party in Bengal. Made Vithalbhai Patel CLA President 1925. Formally part of Congress after Belgaum Dec 1924.

nodes.label: Gaya Congress Session (Dec 1922)
nodes.detail: Annual INC Dec 1922, presided over by C.R. Das. Das and Motilal Nehru moved "mend or end" councils resolution — defeated 1748 vs 890 by No-Changer camp of Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, C. Rajagopalachari. Das and Motilal resigned from Congress offices; announced formation of Swaraj Party within a week. Welcomed AITUC and formed committee to assist its work.

nodes.label: Pro-Changers vs No-Changers (1922-24)
nodes.detail: Post-NCM withdrawal split in Congress. Pro-Changers (Das, Motilal) argued for council entry to fill political void and wreck reforms from within. No-Changers (Gandhi, Patel, Rajendra Prasad, Rajagopalachari) argued for continued boycott and constructive programme. Both agreed mass civil disobedience wasn't possible immediately; differed on non-active-phase politics. Settled Nov 1924: Gandhi signed joint statement with Das/Motilal letting Swaraj Party work in councils on behalf of Congress.

nodes.label: Vithalbhai Patel
nodes.detail: Elder brother of Sardar Patel. Leading Swarajist. Elected first Indian President of Central Legislative Assembly March 1925. Famously told the government: "We want you to carry on the administration of this country by veto and by certification... treat the Government of India Act as a scrap of paper." Also President of Bombay Corporation. Died 1933 in Europe — befriended Bose in exile.

nodes.label: Death of C.R. Das (June 1925)
nodes.detail: 16 June 1925 — C.R. Das died, depriving Swaraj Party of its most charismatic leader and effectively beginning its decline. Also split Bengal Congress leadership into Subhas Bose wing (with Yugantar support) and J.M. Sengupta wing (with Anushilan support).

nodes.label: Belgaum Congress Session (Dec 1924)
nodes.detail: Dec 1924 Congress session — the only one Gandhi personally presided over. Endorsed the Gandhi-Das-Motilal joint statement that Swaraj Party would work in legislatures as an integral part of Congress. Gandhi gave Swarajists majority on his Working Committee. Marked reconciliation of pro-changer and no-changer wings.

nodes.label: Public Safety Bill (1928)
nodes.detail: 1928 government attempt to deport "undesirable" foreign communists suspected of Comintern activity. Opposed by all nationalists — Lajpat Rai ("The greatest danger we are in, is from the capitalists and exploiters"), Motilal Nehru ("Slavery of India, Bill No. 1"), Chaman Lal, and even capitalists Purshottamdas Thakurdas and G.D. Birla. Government unable to pass; responded by arresting 31 Communist/trade union/Left leaders at Meerut (March 1929) for the Meerut Conspiracy Case. Also triggered Bhagat Singh-B.K. Dutt bomb in Assembly 8 April 1929.

nodes.label: Responsivists (1926)
nodes.detail: Faction within Swaraj Party from 1926 that wanted to work the 1919 reforms and hold office wherever possible, shifting from obstruction to cooperation. Joined government in Central Provinces. N.C. Kelkar and M.R. Jayakar key figures; Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya separated from Swaraj Party on Responsivist and communal grounds. Responsivist drift triggered Swaraj Party's March 1926 decision to withdraw from legislatures.

nodes.label: Gandhian Constructive Programme
nodes.detail: Multi-faceted grassroots work during passive phases of national movement: khadi and spinning, national education, Hindu-Muslim unity, anti-untouchability, Adivasi uplift, boycott of foreign cloth. Centred in hundreds of ashrams across India (Vedchi Ashram in Bardoli taluq, Ravishankar Maharaj among Baraiyas in Kheda). Served as recruitment channel for political cadres and the steel frame of Satyagraha phases.

nodes.label: Hindustan Republican Association (HRA, Oct 1924)
nodes.detail: Founded October 1924 at Kanpur by Ramprasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjea and Sachindranath Sanyal. Goal: armed revolution to establish "Federal Republic of the United States of India" with adult franchise. Manifesto stood for "abolition of all systems which make the exploitation of man by man possible". Main action: Kakori Robbery 1925. Reorganised as HSRA in 1928.

nodes.label: Ramprasad Bismil
nodes.detail: Co-founder of HRA 1924. Mastermind of Kakori Robbery 9 Aug 1925. Hanged in Gorakhpur Jail 19 December 1927. Wrote poetry including the revolutionary anthem "Sarfaroshi ki tamanna" and a message from the death cell asking youth to give up revolvers and work in "the open movement", establish Hindu-Muslim unity, and unite under Congress.

nodes.label: Sachindranath Sanyal
nodes.detail: HRA co-founder. Author of Bandi Jivan (Incarcerated Life), which served as the textbook of the revolutionary movement. Twice sentenced to Andamans Cellular Jail (life terms). Linked Bengal and Northern India revolutionary strands.

nodes.label: Kakori Train Robbery (Aug 1925)
nodes.detail: 9 August 1925 — ten HRA men held up the 8-Down train at Kakori near Lucknow, looted official railway cash. Purpose: fund armed revolution. Government crackdown — Kakori Conspiracy Case. Ashfaqulla Khan, Ramprasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri hanged (Dec 1927); 4 sent to Andamans for life; 17 others long terms. Chandrashekhar Azad escaped.

nodes.label: Ashfaqulla Khan
nodes.detail: HRA revolutionary. Key participant in Kakori Robbery Aug 1925. Hanged at Faizabad Jail 19 December 1927. Symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity in the revolutionary movement.

nodes.label: Chandrashekhar Azad
nodes.detail: Joined HRA after Kakori; one of only senior leaders to escape arrest. Overall leader of reorganised HSRA from 1928. Pledged "Azad rahunga, azad maruga" (Shall remain free, shall die free). Died in a shooting encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad, 27 February 1931 — self-shot to avoid capture.

nodes.label: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA, Sept 1928)
nodes.detail: Reconstituted at Ferozeshah Kotla ground, Delhi, 9-10 September 1928. Leaders: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Bejoy Sinha, Shiv Varma, Jaidev Kapur (North India) + Chandrashekhar Azad (overall). Adopted socialism as explicit goal. Major actions: Saunders assassination (Dec 1928), Assembly Bomb (April 1929), Lahore Conspiracy (1929-31). Key document: Philosophy of the Bomb.

nodes.label: Death of Lala Lajpat Rai (Nov 1928)
nodes.detail: 30 October 1928 — "Sher-e-Punjab" Lala Lajpat Rai led anti-Simon Commission demonstration at Lahore. Brutal lathi charge by Scott (Superintendent of Police); blows by J.P. Saunders. Lajpat Rai died 17 November 1928 from injuries. Last words: "Every blow aimed at me today will be a nail in the coffin of British rule." HSRA took vengeance.

nodes.label: Saunders Assassination (Dec 1928)
nodes.detail: 17 December 1928 (note: Bipin Chandra says Nov 17 but historically Dec 17) — HSRA revenge for Lajpat Rai's death. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Chandrashekhar Azad shot dead J.P. Saunders, Assistant Superintendent of Police (mistaken for James Scott who had led the lathi charge). Escaped Lahore with famous poster: "J.P. Saunders is dead. Lala Lajpat Rai is avenged". Led to Lahore Conspiracy Case.

nodes.label: Central Assembly Bomb (April 1929)
nodes.detail: 8 April 1929 — Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw two deliberately-harmless bombs in Central Legislative Assembly in protest against Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill. Leaflet declared "to make the deaf hear". Did not flee; arrested deliberately to use trial as propaganda platform. Inquilab Zindabad slogan popularised. Led to Lahore Conspiracy Case and Bhagat Singh's later hanging.

nodes.label: Batukeshwar Dutt (B.K. Dutt)
nodes.detail: HSRA revolutionary. Threw Assembly bomb with Bhagat Singh 8 April 1929. Arrested deliberately; sentenced to life imprisonment in the Andamans. Released 1938 after failing health. Participated in Quit India 1942. Survived to see independence.

nodes.label: Shivaram Rajguru
nodes.detail: HSRA revolutionary. Participated in Saunders assassination (Dec 1928). Arrested later. Hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931 along with Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev. Famously insisted on going first to the gallows.

nodes.label: Sukhdev Thapar
nodes.detail: Close associate of Bhagat Singh. Co-organiser of Lahore Students Union and Naujawan Bharat Sabha. Tried in Lahore Conspiracy Case. Hanged alongside Bhagat Singh and Rajguru on 23 March 1931.

nodes.label: Jatin Das Hunger-Strike Death (Sept 1929)
nodes.detail: Jatin Das, fellow HSRA revolutionary, joined Bhagat Singh's jail hunger strike demanding that political prisoners be treated differently from ordinary criminals. Died 13 September 1929 on 63rd day of fast. 6-lakh-strong two-mile procession carried his coffin through Calcutta — cemented national sympathy for the revolutionaries.

nodes.label: Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-31)
nodes.detail: Follow-up to Saunders assassination and Assembly bomb — HSRA revolutionaries prosecuted in Lahore. Defiant attitude, Inquilab Zindabad slogans, revolutionary songs ("Sarfaroshi ki tamanna", "Mera rang de basanti chola") won national sympathy. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru sentenced to death — hanged 23 March 1931 at Lahore Central Jail. Country in mourning; Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) could not secure their reprieve.

nodes.label: Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)
nodes.detail: Founded by Bhagat Singh 1926, served as open (legal) wing of HSRA. Carried political work among youth, peasants, workers. Villages branches, magic-lantern political lectures. Six rules included: "have nothing to do with communal bodies" and "create the spirit of general toleration". Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev also organised Lahore Students Union as open youth body.

nodes.label: Philosophy of the Bomb (1930)
nodes.detail: Foundational HSRA ideological document, written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Chandrashekhar Azad and Yashpal. Defined revolution as "independence, social, political and economic aimed at establishing a new order of society in which political and economic exploitation will be an impossibility". Marked HSRA's shift from mere terrorism to socialist revolutionary theory.

nodes.label: Bhagwati Charan Vohra
nodes.detail: HSRA chief ideologue and bomb-maker. Co-author of Philosophy of the Bomb. Died 28 May 1930 while testing a bomb meant to rescue Bhagat Singh from jail — bomb exploded prematurely in his hands on banks of Ravi river.

nodes.label: "Why I am an Atheist" by Bhagat Singh (1930)
nodes.detail: Essay written by Bhagat Singh in Lahore Central Jail, few weeks before his hanging. Critiqued religion and religious philosophy. Traced his path from belief ("mythology and doctrines of Sikhism") to atheism and materialism. Argued revolutionaries need "criticism and independent thinking". Reflected his Marxist turn.

nodes.label: Chittagong Armoury Raid (April 1930)
nodes.detail: 18 April 1930 — 65 revolutionaries in the Indian Republican Army (Chittagong Branch) under Surya Sen seized Chittagong Police Armoury (Ganesh Ghosh) and Auxiliary Force Armoury (Lokenath Baul), cut telegraph/telephone, dislocated rail. Failed to locate ammunition. Surya Sen hoisted National Flag, proclaimed Provisional Revolutionary Government. Retreated to Jalalabad hills; fierce battle 22 April — 80 British troops, 12 revolutionaries died. Villagers sheltered them 3 years. Surya Sen arrested 16 Feb 1933, hanged 12 Jan 1934. Major impact on Bengal youth — 1930-32 revolutionary revival.

nodes.label: Surya Sen (Masterda)
nodes.detail: Leader of Chittagong Armoury Raid. National-school teacher ("Masterda"). Active in NCM 1920-22. Arrested 1926-28. Secretary of Chittagong District Congress 1929. Organiser of the April 1930 raid. Captured 16 Feb 1933, hanged 12 Jan 1934. Included Muslims (Sattar, Mir Ahmad) in his revolutionary cadre — rare departure from Bengal revolutionary Hindu religiosity.

nodes.label: Pritilata Waddedar
nodes.detail: Female revolutionary in Surya Sen's Chittagong group. Led 24 September 1932 raid on Pahartali European Club (sign: "Dogs and Indians not allowed"). Injured during escape; swallowed potassium cyanide to avoid capture. Among the first female martyrs of India's armed struggle.

nodes.label: Kalpana Dutt (Joshi)
nodes.detail: Female revolutionary, Chittagong group under Surya Sen. Arrested and tried alongside Surya Sen, sentenced to transportation for life. Released 1939. Later joined CPI, married P.C. Joshi.

nodes.label: Santi Ghosh & Suniti Chowdhury Shoot DM (Dec 1931)
nodes.detail: 14 December 1931 — two Comilla schoolgirls, Santi Ghosh (14) and Suniti Chowdhury (14), shot and killed District Magistrate C.G.B. Stevens at Comilla. Both imprisoned rather than hanged (juvenile). Emblematic of young women in Bengal revolutionary movement's new phase 1930-32.

nodes.label: Bina Das Fires at Governor (Feb 1932)
nodes.detail: 6 February 1932 — Bina Das fired her pistol at Stanley Jackson, Governor of Bengal, at Calcutta University Convocation. Missed. Sentenced to 9 years rigorous imprisonment. Released 1939. Later participated in Quit India 1942.

nodes.label: Death of Chandrashekhar Azad (Feb 1931)
nodes.detail: 27 February 1931 — at Alfred Park, Allahabad, surrounded by police after a tip-off. After exchange of fire, Azad reportedly shot himself to fulfill his pledge to never be captured alive. Marked the practical end of the HSRA revolutionary phase in North India.

nodes.label: Madras Congress Session (Dec 1927)
nodes.detail: Annual INC session December 1927. Resolved to boycott Simon Commission. Jawaharlal Nehru moved a snap resolution declaring Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the goal — passed in heated atmosphere. Gandhi in Young India 12 Jan 1928 urged action, not just resolutions.

nodes.label: Simon Commission Landing Protests (Feb 1928)
