nodes.detail: Introduced by GoI Act 1935, operational April 1937. Replaced dyarchy. Provinces became autonomous units administered by elected Ministers responsible to provincial Legislative Assembly. Governor retained special powers (discretionary, of individual judgement) over minorities, civil servants, law & order, British business interests. Could take over administration indefinitely. Congress formed ministries in 8 provinces (July 1937). Discontinued when Congress Ministries resigned October 1939 over WWII declaration.

nodes.label: Federal Court of India (1937)
nodes.detail: Established 1 October 1937 under GoI Act 1935 provisions. Supreme judicial body for British India + princely states. First Chief Justice: Sir Maurice Gwyer. Sat in Delhi. Had limited appellate jurisdiction; Privy Council in London remained final court. Replaced 26 January 1950 by Supreme Court of India.

nodes.label: Reserve Bank of India (1935)
nodes.detail: Established 1 April 1935 under GoI Act 1935 and RBI Act 1934 to regulate issue of currency and credit. Originally privately owned; nationalised January 1949. First Governor: Sir Osborne Smith (1935-37). First Indian Governor: C.D. Deshmukh (1943-49). Replaced earlier Imperial Bank of India currency-issuing function. Recommended by 1926 Hilton-Young Commission.

nodes.label: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha (CA Temporary President)
nodes.detail: Oldest member of Constituent Assembly (84). Elected temporary President at first CA meeting on 9 December 1946, following French practice of seating the oldest member as chairman. Dr Rajendra Prasad subsequently elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

nodes.label: Rajendra Prasad elected CA President (Dec 1946)
nodes.detail: 11 December 1946 — Dr Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly. H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari elected Vice-Presidents. Rajendra Prasad chaired the CA when functioning as constitution-making body; G.V. Mavalankar chaired it when functioning as legislative/dominion parliament post-1947. After Constitution came into force 26 Jan 1950, Rajendra Prasad elected first President of Republic of India.

nodes.label: Constituent Assembly Composition (1946-49)
nodes.detail: Originally 389 seats under Cabinet Mission Plan (296 British India + 93 princely states). Indirectly elected by provincial assemblies (July-Aug 1946). INC won 208 of 296 seats; Muslim League 73; small groups/independents 15. Princely-state seats filled gradually after Mountbatten Plan (June 1947). Post-Partition (15 Aug 1947): strength reduced to 299 (229 provinces + 70 princely states) after Muslim League Pakistan members withdrew. Representation: Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, Anglo-Indians, Christians, SCs, STs, women. Notable exception: Mahatma Gandhi was not a member. Limited franchise (only 11-15% of adults voted for provincial assemblies).

nodes.label: Eight Major Committees of Constituent Assembly
nodes.detail: Union Powers Committee (Nehru); Union Constitution Committee (Nehru); Provincial Constitution Committee (Patel); Drafting Committee (Ambedkar); Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal Areas (Patel — had 5 sub-committees including J.B. Kripalani on FR, H.C. Mukherjee on Minorities, A.V. Thakkar on Excluded Areas, Gopinath Bardoloi on NE Tribal); Rules of Procedure Committee (Rajendra Prasad); States Committee for Negotiations (Nehru); Steering Committee (Rajendra Prasad). Plus 13 minor committees. Structure underpinned the three-year constitution-making process.

nodes.label: Drafting Committee — Seven Members (Aug 1947)
nodes.detail: Set up 29 August 1947. Chairman: Dr B.R. Ambedkar. Members: N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Dr K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (replacing B.L. Mitter who resigned), T.T. Krishnamachari (replacing D.P. Khaitan who died 1948). Drafted Constitution in 141 sitting days over less than 6 months. First Draft published Feb 1948; eight months public consultation; Second Draft Oct 1948. Third reading began 14 Nov 1949; passed 26 Nov 1949 (Constitution Day).

nodes.label: B.N. Rau (Constitutional Advisor)
nodes.detail: Benegal Narsing Rau (1887-1953). Constitutional Advisor to Constituent Assembly. Prepared the initial draft of the Constitution October 1947 (studied constitutions of 60+ countries). Rau's draft was the foundation that the Drafting Committee (Ambedkar) worked on. Later India's representative at UN and Judge of International Court of Justice.

nodes.label: M.N. Roy's Idea of Constituent Assembly (1934)
nodes.detail: 1934 — M.N. Roy first articulated the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India. INC officially demanded one in 1935. Nehru declared (1938) that the Constitution of free India "must be framed, without outside interference, by a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise". Accepted in principle by August Offer 1940. Cripps Proposals 1942 elaborated. Cabinet Mission Plan 1946 formulated the scheme actually adopted.

nodes.label: Cabinet Mission — Three-Member Composition (March 1946)
nodes.detail: Three British Cabinet Ministers sent by Attlee government to negotiate Indian constitutional settlement: (1) Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India — leader); (2) Sir Stafford Cripps (President of Board of Trade); (3) A.V. Alexander (First Lord of Admiralty). Arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Plan announced 16 May 1946 — rejected Pakistan demand but proposed three-tier federal structure with Union, three provincial Groups (A: Hindu-majority; B: NW Muslim-majority; C: Bengal+Assam), and provinces. Interim Government formed Sept 1946.

nodes.label: Objectives Resolution — Text & Adoption
nodes.detail: Moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946. Declared: India shall be an Independent Sovereign Republic; territories organised as Union with autonomous units + residuary powers; all power derived from the people; guaranteed justice, equality, freedom of thought/expression/belief/worship; safeguards for minorities and backward classes; integrity of national territory. Unanimously adopted 22 January 1947. Forms basis of the Constitution's Preamble. Marked the philosophical foundation of the new Republic.

nodes.label: August Offer Accepts Constituent Assembly (1940)
nodes.detail: 8 August 1940 — Linlithgow's August Offer to get Indian cooperation in WWII. Though rejected by Congress over concrete demands, it represented the first British acceptance in principle of Indian demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame a new Constitution. Elaborated later in Cripps Proposals 1942 and Cabinet Mission Plan 1946.

nodes.label: Cabinet Mission Plan Three-Tier Federation
nodes.detail: Key innovation of Cabinet Mission Plan May 1946: (1) Union Centre handling only Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications; (2) Three Groups of Provinces — Group A (Hindu-majority: Madras, Bombay, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa); Group B (Muslim-majority NW: Punjab, NWFP, Sind); Group C (Bengal + Assam); (3) Provinces with residual powers, could opt out of Groups after first general election. Princes could federate or stay. Accepted by Muslim League 6 June; Congress accepted with reservations. Collapsed after Nehru's 10 July press conference and League's Direct Action call.

nodes.label: Indian Independence Act — CA Sovereign Changes (1947)
nodes.detail: 15 August 1947 — Indian Independence Act made three changes to Constituent Assembly: (1) Made it a fully sovereign body — could abrogate/alter any British law on India; (2) Assembly also became a legislative body (Dominion Parliament) — separate days for two functions; Rajendra Prasad chaired constitution-making; G.V. Mavalankar chaired legislative sessions; (3) Muslim League members from Pakistan areas withdrew — strength reduced from 389 to 299 (229 provinces + 70 states). CA held 11 sessions over 2 years, 11 months, 18 days. Final Constitution adopted 26 November 1949, came into force 26 January 1950.

nodes.label: Constitution Adopted (26 November 1949)
nodes.detail: 26 November 1949 — Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India. Ambedkar moved the motion: "the Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed". 284 of 299 members signed. Preamble declares "We, the people of India... do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution". Observed as Constitution Day from 2015. Some articles (citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament) came into immediate effect; rest came into force 26 January 1950 (Republic Day, echoing 1930 Poorna Swaraj pledge).
